assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology is a rare case in which basic hormone biology led directly to transformative therapies: incretin effects, proglucagon processing, and the actions of GLP-1 on islets, appetite and gastric emptying underlie drugs that have changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. The discovery is clear, original and has enormous, measurable impact on patients.
assessment.attribution: Several people made decisive contributions: Holst and Drucker for physiology and pharmacology of GLP-1 and GLP-2, Mojsov for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide forms, and Knudsen for medicinal chemistry (liraglutide, semaglutide). I favour the three basic-science contributors, and recognise the allocation is contested; Knudsen's industrial drug-development role could alternatively be the third slot. Habener and others are not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of mechanistic work, large independent cardiovascular and metabolic outcome trials, and wide clinical adoption make recognition timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Holst, Drucker, Mojsov, Knudsen and uncredited contributors is disputed.
Whether the committee prefers recognising physiology versus drug development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new treatment modality, achieving durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and now myeloma. A clear conceptual and clinical breakthrough with substantial lasting impact on cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain led the design and clinical translation of CD19 CAR constructs with costimulatory domains (CD28, 4-1BB) and first pivotal clinical responses. Rosenberg contributed key early clinical cell therapy and CAR trials, but the core design work is best covered by two. Eshhar's earlier chimeric receptor concept is not in the supplied list and may complicate a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products since 2017 and multiple years of follow-up demonstrate durable responses; recognition is timely though long-term toxicity and solid tumour limits remain.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept versus clinical translation is unresolved.
Efficacy in solid tumours is unproven; long-term safety (secondary malignancies) is still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) turned a lethal infant neurodegenerative disease into a treatable one, and established a general framework for splice-modulating oligonucleotide therapy. The mechanistic insight and the clinical outcome are both clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing silencer elements and the mechanism of SMN2 exon 7 skipping; Bennett developed the antisense chemistry and drug platform with the clinical programme. The pairing is natural and supports a clean two-person configuration, though others (e.g. Hua, Singh, Adrian, clinical investigators) contributed.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of real-world follow-up; confirmed by independent trials and by subsequent RNA therapeutics. Timely, perhaps slightly early relative to the longest-term evidence.
uncertainties: Relative weight of the mechanistic splicing discovery versus oligonucleotide chemistry is arguable.
Competition with other SMA therapies (gene therapy, risdiplam) may dilute the attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade produces clinical benefit in rheumatoid arthritis opened the biologic era for inflammatory disease. The concept was tested by clear clinical trials and extended to Crohn's disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly performed the translational work from human synovial cytokine biology to anti-TNF trials and are consistently paired. Other contributors (Vilcek, Cerami and Beutler on TNF itself, Kollias, Tracey) are not supplied for this candidate, which may create an incomplete credit picture.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: more than two decades of independent confirmation and a major class of therapeutics. If anything the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Broader TNF discovery credit (cachectin, cloning) may require a separate recognition.
Whether the committee views this as primarily therapeutic rather than fundamental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type specific control of neural activity and transformed neuroscience research, with applications from circuit analysis to vision restoration. The discovery of channelrhodopsins and their use in neurons are original, with huge methodological impact.
assessment.attribution: This is a compound discovery with many contributors: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann for channelrhodopsin characterisation; Boyden and Deisseroth for neuronal expression and application; Miesenbock for early genetic photostimulation. With at most three laureates, I pick Deisseroth for neuronal deployment and Nagel and Hegemann for channelrhodopsin discovery, leaving Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenbock aside; this is a genuine difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated for over a decade; clinical translation is just beginning with early retinal trials, so the tool impact is mature while therapeutic impact is emerging.
uncertainties: Six credible contributors versus a three-person limit.
Whether a tool or method is weighed as a physiological or medical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling pathway from ER to nucleus (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK) and links proteostasis to disease, including diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A coherent, fundamental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and jointly identified the Ire1 and HAC1 mRNA splicing mechanism and the transcriptional response; the pair is a natural, well-defined configuration. Others such as Kaufman, Ron and Schekman-linked work on ER stress may contest completeness.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation across yeast and mammals. Disease relevance is still being translated into therapies, so impact is mostly conceptual.
uncertainties: Contributions of Ron, Kaufman and Shen on the PERK and ATF6 arms may be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent infection and precancerous lesions, and population data now show declines in cervical disease. A clear and highly consequential preventive-medicine advance, building on the link between HPV and cervical cancer already recognised in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs and demonstrated their immunogenicity; Frazer and the late Jian Zhou developed the VLP and vaccine technology in parallel. Zhou's death complicates a fair allocation, and the three credited names are reasonable under that constraint.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with strong real-world evidence of reduced cervical cancer incidence in vaccinated cohorts. Timely.
uncertainties: Posthumous contribution of Jian Zhou is not creditable in the supplied list.
Patent and priority disputes over VLP technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death, founding the field of apoptosis regulation by the BCL-2 family and leading to BH3 mimetic therapies such as venetoclax. A fundamental and clinically validated discovery.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory defined the BCL-2 family and its role in lymphoma and survival signalling; Vaux showed BCL-2 prolongs survival without promoting proliferation. Strasser also contributed to the family. Earlier work by Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Cleary on the translocation is not in the supplied credit, so attribution is not clean. Part of the field was recognised in the 2002 prize (Sulston, Brenner, Horvitz) for programmed cell death in C. elegans.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of mechanistic and clinical confirmation; venetoclax gives strong therapeutic validation.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize and priority of Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Cleary.
